stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that \( x(t) = t + 4 \ln{\left(t^{2} + 1 \right)} \) and \( y'(t) = e^{\frac{t}{3}} \sin{\left(t \right)} \) for \( t \ge 0 \). Using a calculator, find the acceleration vector of the particle at \( t = \frac{5}{2} \). Show the setup for the calculations, and give each value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The component given as a velocity is differentiated once, \( \frac{e^{\frac{t}{3}} \sin{\left(t \right)}}{3} + e^{\frac{t}{3}} \cos{\left(t \right)} \) at \( t = \frac{5}{2} \) gives about -1.384.
The component given as a position is differentiated twice, \( - \frac{8 \left(t - 1\right) \left(t + 1\right)}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{2}} \) at \( t = \frac{5}{2} \) gives about -0.799.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative of a position component

options.label: \( \left\langle 3.759, -1.384 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: each given component differentiated once, so the position component yields its velocity, not its acceleration

options.label: \( \left\langle -1.384, -0.799 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: the two components written in the wrong order

options.label: \( \left\langle 3.759, 1.377 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: the velocity vector at the time reported as the acceleration
